QGARS: neutral-atom reservoir computing with a guided autoencoder [](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.06727) [](https://doi.org/10.1109/QAI63978.2025.00064) [](requirements.txt) [](LICENSE) Code for the paper *Medical Imaging Classification with Cold-Atom Reservoir Computing using Auto-Encoders and Surrogate-Driven Training* (IEEE QAI 2025; free on arXiv). QGARS (Quantum Guided Autoencoder with Reservoir Surrogate) compresses each image with an autoencoder, writes the latent code into the local detunings of a simulated chain of Rydberg atoms, and classifies the measured correlations with a linear classifier. Measurements block gradients, so a small neural network (the surrogate) learns to imitate the reservoir, which lets the classification loss train the encoder. (a) Autoencoder. (b) Rydberg-atom reservoir. (c) Surrogate, retrained every $N$ e
